title: First-to-third grip trial change does not improve elevated-HbA1c discrimination across independent NHANES cycles
abstract: A source-frozen bilateral normalized first-to-third grip decline did not improve HbA1c>=6.5% discrimination beyond maximum and weight-normalized grip plus demographic/BMI measures: target deltaAUC -0.001542, paired95%CI [-0.003347, +0.000304]; Brier worsened. This is a bounded negative predictive test, not evidence of no muscle fatigability mechanism. Source2011-12 n4402/521 cases, target2013-14 n4893/511. Source fivefold deltaAUC+0.000213; frozen target AUC0.796411 versus0.794869. Joint-refit interval also included zero; no-pain, maximal-effort, nonlinear-baseline and survey-weighted checks did not rescue transfer. No causal, clinical-equivalence or globally novel biomarker claim.
